Indirect payments and reimbursements through federal and state government programs have never fully compensated public and private hospitals for the full cost of care mandated by EMTALA.

Main.id: Healthcare in the United States - Wikipedia#205
Main.sentence: More than half of all emergency care in the US now goes uncompensated.

Main.id: Healthcare in the United States - Wikipedia#206
Main.sentence: According to some analyses, EMTALA is an unfunded mandate that has contributed to financial pressures on hospitals in the last 20 years, causing them to consolidate and close facilities, and contributing to emergency room overcrowding.

Main.id: Healthcare in the United States - Wikipedia#207
Main.sentence: According to the ___E:Institute of Medicine U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Institute_of_Medicine)___ , between 1993 and 2003, emergency room visits in the US grew by 26%, while in the same period, the number of emergency departments declined by 425.

Main.id: Healthcare in the United States - Wikipedia#208
Main.sentence: Mentally ill patients present a unique challenge for emergency departments and hospitals.

Main.id: Healthcare in the United States - Wikipedia#209
Main.sentence: In accordance with EMTALA, mentally ill patients who enter emergency rooms are evaluated for emergency medical conditions.

Main.id: Healthcare in the United States - Wikipedia#210
Main.sentence: Once mentally ill patients are medically stable, regional mental health agencies are contacted to evaluate them. Patients are evaluated as to whether they are a danger to themselves or others.

Main.id: Healthcare in the United States - Wikipedia#211
Main.sentence: Those meeting this criterion are admitted to a mental health facility to be further evaluated by a psychiatrist.

Main.id: Healthcare in the United States - Wikipedia#212
Main.sentence: Typically, mentally ill patients can be held for up to 72 hours, after which a court order is required.

Main.id: Healthcare in the United States - Wikipedia#213
Main.sentence: Healthcare quality assurance consists of the "activities and programs intended to assure or improve the quality of care in either a defined medical setting or a program.

Main.id: Healthcare in the United States - Wikipedia#214

Private companies such as ___E:Grand Rounds U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Grand_Rounds,_Inc.&action=edit&redlink=1)___ also release quality information and offer services to employers and plans to map quality within their networks.

Main.id: Healthcare in the United States - Wikipedia#215

Main.id: Healthcare in the United States - Wikipedia#217
